solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mafia's activity in central America?

parts.note: the Mafia's business is crime run as a structured enterprise; the question mark flags the play on 'central', as in the crime being centrally run and the Mafia's American heartland

explanation.surface: A question about what gangsters get up to in the middle of the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central America' looks like the isthmus between Mexico and Colombia; read instead as a hint at crime that is centrally run, the hallmark of the Mafia in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the standard term for criminal enterprise run by syndicates such as the Mafia.

clue.text: Like actors, if twice involved in all-out effort?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these words are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Asks whether actors are like a huge collective push if they get involved twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word, 'Like', looks like a link but belongs to the fodder: LIKE, ACTORS and IF, used twice as 'twice' instructs, are shuffled together, signalled by 'involved'.
explanation.definitionFit: A union-backed stoppage where every member walks out is 'all out', a punning take on a total effort.

clue.text: Person of refined taste partly improving our method

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone of discerning taste is helping to refine our way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet is a connoisseur of food and drink, someone whose palate is discriminating.

clue.text: Madly into animals, hence partiality for the country

indicators.note: madly means wildly and chaotically, so the letters of the following words are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone charges wildly into a herd of beasts, and so shows a love of the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationalism is strong devotion to and favouritism towards one's own nation.

clue.text: Confession from ring-leader secured by group of workers

indicators.note: secured by means held fast inside, so the letter goes within the group of workers

parts.note: a shift is a team of workers on duty together

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of ring

parts.note: its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A confession extracted from the ringleader of a gang held by labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring-leader' looks like one word for a gang boss, but it splits: the leader of 'ring' is R, held inside SHIFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrift is the old word for confession to a priest and absolution, surviving in 'short shrift'.

clue.text: No-win situation holding no more excitement

parts.note: something that is no more is dead
heat is passion or excitement, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A stalemate in which nothing thrilling happens any more.
explanation.definitionFit: A race where competitors finish level produces no single winner, a tie.

clue.text: Sailor picked up, one escaping doomed ship

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means lifted, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is rescued while one man flees a sinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests rescue or a homophone, but in a down answer it means turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are proverbially said to desert a sinking ship, hence a deserter or turncoat.

clue.text: Daisy's family member is in my control

indicators.note: is in means placed inside, so the flower goes within the following word

parts.note: taken as written
the aster belongs to the daisy family of plants

explanation.surface: A relative of someone called Daisy falls under the speaker's power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' reads as a woman's name, but it is the flower; the aster is a member of the daisy family.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastery is command or dominance over something, full control.

clue.text: Pomposity spoiling a PM's reflection

indicators.note: spoiling means ruining, so the letters of the following words are broken up and reordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Pompousness is ruining the Prime Minister's image.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-importance is an inflated sense of one's own worth, the essence of pomposity.

clue.text: Bet pound on favourite initially, say

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, puts the pound after the favourite's letter, placed next to it
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: its first letter is taken
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: A punter backs the favourite with a pound, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb UTTER; L (pound) sits on F, the first letter of 'favourite'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flutter is a small wager, British slang for a modest gamble.

clue.text: Stage performer in part is terrific

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: An actor's role turns out to be wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Almost made it in academic stream?

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: came means arrived, made it

explanation.surface: Nearly succeeded within an educational track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stream' suggests a school set or class; it is a river, the Cam that flows through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cam is the river at Cambridge, so a university watercourse.

clue.text: Immediately available to be married?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ready-made stock, bought without ordering
second meaning: no longer 'on the shelf', the old phrase for a woman thought past marrying

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense plays on 'on the shelf', an old-fashioned phrase for someone unlikely to marry; once wed, they are off it.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold ready-made from stock, rather than custom-made, are bought this way.

clue.text: Unrehearsed, awful panto's no use

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, signalling the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An unprepared performance proves the dreadful pantomime is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a pantomime, the British Christmas stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spontaneous happens on impulse, without planning or practice.

clue.text: Heads off East — or way off course

indicators.note: heads off means each word loses its opening letter

parts.note: loses its first letter
loses its first letter
loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Travellers set out eastward, or else wander far from their route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' looks like setting out, but it beheads each of East, or and way, leaving AST, R and AY.
explanation.definitionFit: To go astray is to wander from the right path or route.

clue.text: Stand-in NCO securing area in sudden attack

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the outer letters grip the next piece

parts.note: a proxy is a substitute acting for someone
SM is a sergeant major, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A substitute sergeant holds ground during a surprise raid.
explanation.walkthrough: NCO is a non-commissioned officer; SM (sergeant major) is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A paroxysm is a sudden violent outburst or fit, such as of coughing or rage.

clue.text: End to travel, as Waterloo was

parts.note: a close is a conclusion or end
to run is to travel, as a bus runs

explanation.surface: A journey's end, compared with the famous battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington called the Battle of Waterloo 'the nearest-run thing'; the phrase is popularly quoted as 'a damn close-run thing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest decided by a narrow margin, as the 1815 battle famously was.

clue.text: Provide with translation, in a way, being nuanced about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word goes round the following piece

parts.note: subtle means finely nuanced
taken as written

explanation.surface: Giving a text in another language, in a manner that is sensitive to shades of meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtitle a film is to add captions translating the dialogue.

clue.text: Inclined to sell, as to carry on is hard

parts.note: to bear is to carry
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Reluctance to keep going is a tough thing, an investor might say.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the carrying word sits over the rest; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearish trader expects prices to fall and so is keen to sell, a stock-market sense.

clue.text: Returned shares with company that goes to the wall

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: cuts are shares, as in a cut of the profits

explanation.surface: Shares come back along with a firm that has gone bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to the wall' suggests a failing company, but it is literal: plaster applied to walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is plaster or render spread on the outside of walls.

clue.text: Is able to preserve a Spanish bar

parts.note: can means is able
to tin food is to preserve it in a can

explanation.surface: Someone manages to keep a Spanish pub going.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantina is the Spanish word for a tavern or bar.

clue.text: Reflect about one's inappropriate application

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to muse is to reflect or ponder
I is one, so one's is IS

explanation.surface: Think about whether someone's use of something is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse is the wrong or improper use of something.

clue.text: Interpret objective as getting in again

parts.note: to read is to interpret
a mission is a goal or objective

explanation.surface: Understanding a target as a matter of re-entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Readmission is being allowed to enter again, as to a hospital or club.

clue.text: Head organised teachers, initially

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for the head
second meaning: the initials of the National Union of Teachers, a UK trade union

explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain, an organised body of teachers; 'initially' says it is an acronym.
explanation.definitionFit: Nut is informal slang for the head, as in 'use your nut'.

clue.text: Follower of pattern, typically, making unusual trinket

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who follows a design creates an odd little ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follower of pattern' sounds like a conformist; it is someone working from a knitting pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitter typically works from a printed pattern of stitches.

clue.text: In tug of war, starts to pull

indicators.note: starts means the opening letters, one from each word

parts.note: first letter taken
first letter taken
first letter taken

explanation.surface: A tug-of-war team begins heaving on the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow is to pull something behind, as a vehicle on a rope.

clue.text: You expressed a point that's crazy and idealistic

indicators.note: expressed means spoken, so the word is the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the word you is said aloud, and sounds like the letter U

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend their argument is mad and unrealistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes visionary schemes for a perfect society, impractical ideals.

clue.text: Story of one season's play

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, a tale belonging to a single time of year
second meaning: Shakespeare's late romance of that name

explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading describes a tale of a cold-weather season; it is also the title of a Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Shakespeare romance featuring Leontes, Hermione and the famous bear.
